frozen_note: Frozen before any call and before the build (coordinator GO 2026-11-27 after the offline diff gate SURVIVED: wrong flagged 8/19, correct 2/49). The two arm plans (CODING_DIFFGATE_CONTROL_PLAN.json, CODING_DIFFGATE_GATE_PLAN.json) are generated from this file and differ only in their arm fields.
question: Does a live differential-consensus gate on top of the public-test gate cut wrong coding answers at an acceptable cost in solved cases and energy?
cases: coding-hard-v1 evaluation split, 24 tasks x fresh seeds 70-78 = 216 cases per arm (no earlier plan or run used seeds >= 67 on this corpus); agent_seed_offset 70700 (unused); both arms the same cases and offset
control: the production coding default exactly as CODING_BASELINE_PLAN.json / CODING_BASELINE_S64_PLAN.json: run_coding_earlystop.py, early stop first_feedback_pass_in_time, R2 rolling width 2 up to 8 code_elastic agents, worker source .runtime/coding-reserve-source @2b0195e, the same limits, scheduling (20 agents per node), serving identity and transport retries as production

gate.runner: run_coding_diffgate.py (the control's runner and worker, plus the gate below; nothing else changes)
gate.passer: an agent whose final proposal passes ALL public feedback tests (the control's acceptance test); its code is the trace's puzzle_end code
gate.distinct: passers with byte-identical code (sha256) count once: a later identical passer neither votes nor counts
gate.no_early_accept: a public-test pass does NOT end the case; it counts as an ended agent for the rolling replacement (like a failure), so agents keep starting up to the existing cap of 8
gate.generator: at the case's first passer: one generator call with the frozen generic prompt of DIFFGATE_PLAN.json (system and user text, payload {function_name, spec} only), thinking 8,192 then the forced answer within 10,240 in total, on the endpoint of the passer that triggers it (its worker thread runs the call, so no node exceeds its per-node request cap); the reply's code block runs in the sandbox (generate mode, 10 s) to give the inputs (first 64); if the inputs are unusable, ONE more generator call; if still unusable the case uses the fallback below
gate.sandbox: each distinct passer runs on the inputs in the CPU-only Docker sandbox (inkling/sandbox_outputs.py, reviewed: fleet hosts Spark_01-04 only with verified host and daemon identity, host-side deadline, output cap and label-verified cleanup) on the case's host (agent-0 slot), 2 s per input, 60 s per program; its behaviour is the vector of outcome sha256 (exceptions and timeouts are outcomes); a passer that cannot be loaded or exceeds 60 s has no behaviour and never votes
gate.vote: behaviour classes are identical outcome vectors; after each distinct passer's behaviour is known, the case is ACCEPTED as soon as one class holds >= 2 distinct passers; the answer is the class member that passed first (in time); the case's other agents are then terminated and queued ones never start, as in the control
gate.fallback: if no usable inputs exist after two generator calls, the case is accepted when it has 2 distinct passers (agreement on the public tests only); such cases are reported as fallback
gate.abstain: if all 8 agents have ended and no class holds >= 2 distinct passers (including cases with fewer than 2 distinct passers), the case is UNANSWERED (abstention)
gate.faults: a generator transport fault or a sandbox infrastructure fault (ssh, docker, host identity, protocol) is a fault of the run (stop admissions, as worker faults), never an acceptance; the generator client has retries 0, terminal usage required and the stop fence at dispatch (research/diffgate-v1)
gate.accounting: generator completion tokens and sandbox container seconds per case and per arm, extra agents (started beyond what the case needed in the control is not observable; reported: agents started per case), votes per case

execution: each arm alone on the fleet via inkling/diffgate_arms.py (the reviewed suspend_arms.py controls: fleet lease, freeze and code-pin checks, admission bound to the plan sha, source revision and canonical endpoints, raw idle gauges before the start, latch-only signals with the runner stopped and reaped, fenced drain before the lease is released, GPU energy for the arm window); arm order control, gate

decision_rule.pass: PASS iff wrong(gate) <= 0.6 x wrong(control) AND solved(gate) >= solved(control) - 3 AND GPU Wh per solved case(gate) <= 1.5 x control (unrounded; energy covering all four nodes)
decision_rule.wrong: an answered case whose answer fails the hidden holdout tests
decision_rule.reported: solved, wrong, unanswered, agents started, generator tokens, sandbox seconds, wall, server generated tokens, Wh per solved, fallback cases, and SHARED-BUG cases separately (gate arm: every distinct passer agreed and the accepted answer is still wrong: the known blind spot)
decision_rule.incomplete: INCOMPLETE (no decision) unless both arms are complete: each run embeds its plan, the plans differ only in arm fields, no runner errors, cases exactly the frozen 216 task x seed keys, runner exit 0, drain confirmed, no signal, energy covering all four nodes

amendment: 2026-11-27, during the build and before any call: the generator call runs on the triggering passer's endpoint instead of the case's agent-0 endpoint, so the per-node request cap of 20 holds.
